NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to prevent shock-induced stiction in MEMS capacitive accelerometer comb structures by introducing a controlled electrostatic repulsion pulse between comb fingers during shock events. Standard practice relies on mechanical design and coatings to prevent contact; this mitigation departs by using a timed electrostatic pulse to actively repel fingers before contact occurs, driven by shock-sensing and a simple RC timing circuit. The closest existing practice is electrostatic actuation in MEMS, but this is used for intentional motion, not as a stiction-prevention repulsion pulse triggered by shock. The mechanism exploits the Coulomb force (F = k*q1*q2/r²) to generate repulsive force sufficient to separate fingers.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the electrostatic repulsion force between charged comb fingers: F_repulsion = ε₀*A*V²/(2*d²), where ε₀ is permittivity, A is overlap area, V is applied voltage, and d is gap. For a 100 V pulse across a 2 µm gap with 100 µm² overlap, F ≈ 2.2 µN, exceeding typical stiction forces (<0.5 µN). This force accelerates fingers apart at >1000 g, preventing contact during shock.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (a) Existing MEMS comb structure; (b) Commercial voltage comparator IC (e.g., LM393, stock grade); (b) Commercial Zener diode (5.1 V, stock grade); (b) Commercial resistor (100 kΩ, stock grade); (b) Commercial capacitor (100 nF, stock grade); (c) Procedure: Connect shock sensor output to comparator input, set threshold at 5000 g; connect comparator output to MEMS electrode via Zener-limited 100 V pulse (10 µs duration, triggered at shock onset).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice: mechanical redesign (high burden). This intervention: adds only 4 catalog components (same class as existing control ICs) and 1 parameter setting (pulse voltage/duty). Installation: 0 (uses existing MEMS electrodes and supply). Commissioning: 1 (parameter programming vs. mechanical redesign). Operational burden: same (no power penalty, pulse is transient). Maintenance: same (no new failure modes). Burden class: same as standard practice (component-level addition, no development).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Subject 10 devices to 10000 g shock (x/y/z axes) with and without intervention. Instruments: Precision shaker, laser interferometer, offset measurement circuit. Pass/fail: Zero-g offset ≤50 mg post-shock in all axes. Duration: 100 shocks per device. Kill criterion: Any device exceeds 50 mg offset. Falsification: If intervention group shows same or higher failure rate vs. control, mechanism fails.
